name: Django Oscar
title: Django Oscar SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce
description: Svelte Commerce on Django Oscar through django-oscar-api: 15 of 43 services wired, with cart, checkout and sign-in; nine gaps, search among them.
lede: The Django Oscar connector is wired against django-oscar-api, a separate package from Oscar core that must be installed and routed on your instance. Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; search is among nine recorded gaps.
verdict: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; coupons, reviews, search, CMS pages, payment-method listing, currencies, states, wishlist and vendors are not. Without search, shoppers find products only by browsing.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your Oscar site

env.name: PUBLIC_DJANGO_OSCAR_API_URL
env.note: Base URL of your Oscar site, with django-oscar-api routed. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_DJANGO_OSCAR_API_KEY
env.note: HTTP Basic username, for stores that authenticate that way. By default the connector uses django-oscar-api’s `Session-Id` header session. See the limitations.

env.name: PUBLIC_DJANGO_OSCAR_API_SECRET
env.note: HTTP Basic password, with the username above.

env.name: PUBLIC_DJANGO_OSCAR_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: Sent as `Authorization: Token <key>` — only useful if your store wired up DRF token authentication itself; django-oscar-api does not ship it.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/oscar-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: The package is `oscar-connector`, but the variables follow the product: `PUBLIC_DJANGO_OSCAR_*`. `init.ts` hands the connector every one that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_DJANGO_OSCAR_ACCESS_KEY`, `PUBLIC_DJANGO_OSCAR_STORE_ID` and `PUBLIC_DJANGO_OSCAR_CHANNEL_ID`; the connector’s source does not read them.
backendSettings: Install django-oscar-api and route it on your instance: it is a separate package from Oscar core, and the connector talks to nothing else.
howItWorks: The connector speaks django-oscar-api, not Oscar core. By default it keeps the shopper’s session in django-oscar-api’s `Session-Id` header, which needs no CSRF token; HTTP Basic works too, and there is no bearer scheme at all — django-oscar-api ignores `Authorization: Bearer`. The route documentation its authors were given was dead, so it was written from the package’s source.
limitations: If you set `PUBLIC_DJANGO_OSCAR_API_KEY` and `PUBLIC_DJANGO_OSCAR_API_SECRET` for HTTP Basic, that username and password reach every visitor: SvelteKit sends `PUBLIC_` variables to the browser.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “the oscar connector is active but PUBLIC_DJANGO_OSCAR_API_URL is not set”
troubleshooting.fix: Add `PUBLIC_DJANGO_OSCAR_API_URL` to `.env`. A production Node build and Docker read `PUBLIC_*` from the process environment rather than `.env`, so set it on your deploy platform too.

troubleshooting.problem: The build stops with “Several commerce connectors are installed … Set PUBLIC_CONNECTOR to pick one”
troubleshooting.fix: More than one `@misiki/*-connector` is in `package.json` and none is Litekart’s. Uninstall the ones you do not run — a fresh clone also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector` — or set `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR='@misiki/oscar-connector'`.

troubleshooting.problem: `[oscar] no native implementation for get /api/...` in the console
troubleshooting.fix: The connector’s REST guard caught a path inherited from Litekart and answered it empty instead of requesting it. Each path is reported once. Harmless if Django Oscar has no such feature; if it has one, the fix belongs in the connector’s matching service.

faq.q: Can I run a Django Oscar store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired through django-oscar-api. Nine services are not, search among them. Like every connector, it has not been run against a live production Oscar store.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to Django Oscar?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/oscar-connector`, set `PUBLIC_DJANGO_OSCAR_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: Does Django Oscar need anything extra installed?
faq.a: Yes: django-oscar-api, a separate package from Oscar core, installed and routed on your instance. The connector talks to it and to nothing else.

openQuestion: Is a headless storefront a supported use case for django-oscar-api? Worth stating either way in its docs.

api.surface: The connector calls the JSON REST API of the `django-oscar-api` package, a Django REST Framework API mounted by the store owner, conventionally under `/api/`, and checked against the package’s `oscarapi/urls.py` and views on master and tag 3.2.4.
api.auth: By default the connector generates a `Session-Id` header of the form `SID:ANON:{host}:{id}`, sends it on every call and captures the copy the server echoes back; signing in is `POST /api/login/` with `username` and `password`, after which the connector flips the header from `ANON` to `AUTH` itself, because a browser can read the echoed header only if the store exposes it.

calls.what: `GET /api/products/` with `page` and `page_size`, then for each row `GET /api/products/{id}/` and the `price` and `availability` links it carries
`GET /api/categories/`, `GET /api/categories/{id}/` for a numeric ID, and the parent path such as `GET /api/categories/books/` to find a category by slug
`GET /api/basket/`, `POST /api/basket/add-product/` with `{ url, quantity }`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /api/baskets/{id}/lines/{lineId}/`, and `POST /api/basket/add-voucher/` with `vouchercode`
`POST /api/login/`, `GET /api/login/` for the signed-in user, `DELETE /api/login/` to sign out, and `POST /api/register/`

rules: Every path ends in a slash, with any query string after it, because Django otherwise answers with a 301 redirect and the POST body is lost.

Relations are absolute URLs in both directions, so the connector adds to the basket with `{ url: <product URL>, quantity }` and checks out with `{ basket: <basket URL> }`; sending `product_id` instead returns 406.

django-oscar-api sets no pagination on any list view, so a stock store returns the whole collection as a bare array and ignores `?page=`; the connector then slices pages itself, and reads `count` from a `{ count, next, previous, results }` envelope only when the store has configured one.

The product list returns only `url`, `id`, `upc` and `title` by default and accepts no search, sort or category filter, so the connector fetches each product’s detail, price and availability separately.

Signing in on a session that is already `AUTH` answers 405 “Session is in use, log out first”, so the connector sends `DELETE /api/login/` first and starts a fresh anonymous session; the `host` part of the header must match the API host without its port, or the store answers 403.
